# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Cross-copy brittleness | 374-9, 52216, 53161 (t1) | Final code block is replayed unchanged on 3 workbook copies with DIFFERENT data; agent hardcodes copy-1 values/positions/counts, or relies on cached formula results (`data_only=True` → `None` on un-recalculated copies) so sums silently drop terms | KNOWLEDGE / STRUCTURE | Additive robustness rules (locate dynamically, guard None caches) |
| 2 | Type / precision mismatch | 418-29, 52216, 347-49 (secondary) | Unconditional `float()`/`round()` writes a float where a whole number is expected, or spurious rounding → graded as mismatch though the number "looks right" | OUTPUT-CONTRACT | Explicit type-match rule + verify-types checklist |
| 3 | Boundary/interval interpretation | 32468 | "including the subsequent 12 months" read as exclusive 12-bucket window → off-by-one; only the terminal cell (where both interpretations converge) matched (30/31 wrong) | KNOWLEDGE | Inclusive-endpoint reading note |
| 4 | Row-deletion calibration | 347-49 | Under-deletes rows vs gold (leaves repeated header/separator rows); fixed-range grading shifts all rows below → cascade of mismatches. Partly idiosyncratic | interpretive (partial) | Folded into type-preservation + boundary/example note |
| — | Infra timeouts (IGNORED) | 55457, 47484, and 418-29 t0/t1 | `sandbox exec failed: Read timed out` — environment noise, mean ~0; NOT a capability defect | ENVIRONMENT | none (handed back) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | missing-rule (KNOWLEDGE) + None-guard | prompt.md | "Beware missing cached formula results": when reading source cells that are formulas, `data_only` returns `None` on some copies — check for unexpected None/blank and recompute from inputs, never treat as 0. General: applies to any source-formula read. | Yes — 40467/160-6 read no formula source cells, so the None-check is a no-op for them |
| 1 | missing-rule / structure | task_template.md | New "make your solution work on all three graded copies" section: don't hardcode values/indices/counts seen only in this copy; locate tables by header text + real data extent; find boundaries dynamically. | Yes — 40467/160-6 already inspect each run and pass 3/3; guidance only reinforces data-driven code |
| 2 | output-contract | prompt.md | "Match the EXPECTED VALUE TYPE and precision exactly": int not `5.0`, no unrequested rounding, text stays text, real dates; wrong-type/rounded value is a mismatch. | Yes — 40467 writes strings ("keep text as text"), 160-6 copies values as-is; neither coerces |
| 2 | structure (unavoidable check) | task_template.md | Verify step 3 upgraded: for EVERY cell in answer_position print value AND Python type; confirm presence, expected type, and nothing written outside range. Makes the type/range check a precondition of finishing. | Yes — passing tasks already verify by re-opening; added assertions pass for their correct outputs |
| 3 | knowledge (interpretation) | prompt.md | "Interpret ranges and boundaries from the wording/example": "including the subsequent N" = anchor + N (inclusive endpoint); re-read example for in/out. | Yes — 40467/160-6 involve no date/interval windows; bounded/additive |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those inputs)
- 374-9 (t1/t2, 16/32 col-B cells LOW on copies 2/3): the summed source column is a formula-total whose cached value is `None` on non-Excel-saved copies, so terms dropped. New None-guard rule → agent detects the blank and recomputes the total from its component columns, giving the same value on all 3 copies. Passing 40467/160-6 read no formula cells → no behavior change.
- 52216 (1/10 differs on copies 2/3, "CHANGED although expected value is the cell's own original input"): agent pasted a copy-1 literal into a dropdown-dependent row it shouldn't have touched. Cross-copy rule ("don't paste a number you saw; leave already-correct cells; compute from run-time data") + "modify ONLY the answer cells" → agent stops hardcoding the snapshot.
- 418-29 (t2, 1/14 "float where int expected, HIGHER"): unconditional `float()`+`round`. Type-match rule ("whole number as int, no unrequested rounding") + verify-types check would surface the float-vs-int before finishing. Passing tasks unaffected (no coercion).
- 53161 (t1, 85/208 wrong): hardcoded fixed row/col offsets; passing trials located tables by label. Cross-copy "locate by header text, find boundaries dynamically" rule pushes toward the approach the passing trials already used.
- 32468 (30/31 wrong, only terminal cell matches): off-by-one window boundary. Inclusive-endpoint rule directs re-reading "including the subsequent N months". Moderate-confidence (interpretive) but bounded/additive; terminal-cell-only-match is the supporting evidence.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: fanned out 4 parallel read-only general-purpose subagents — one on 347-49, one on 374-9+32468, one on 52216+418-29+53161, one on the two passing tasks (40467, 160-6) to map the protected blast radius. Synthesized their reports into the clusters above.
- Prior iterations: none — this is the first optimization iteration (LEDGER shows baseline only; ./prior_iterations/ empty).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The global rule "prefer LITERAL values over live formulas" is LOAD-BEARING for 40467 (a formula there produces wrong serial-number output) and 160-6. Subagents suggested flipping it to "write live formulas" — that is an UNBOUNDED global-decision change that would regress 40467. Do NOT flip it. My cross-copy fix is scoped to READING source formula caches, not to writing the answer as a formula.
- 160-6 depends on writing explicit blanks (None) inside its range — never add a rule forbidding blank cells or demanding every cell be non-empty.
- The strict "modify ONLY answer_position" constraint and the inspect→write→verify multi-round loop.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 55457, 47484: infrastructure timeouts (`sandbox exec failed: Read timed out`), mean ~0 — environment noise, not prompt-fixable. Also 418-29 t0/t1 (same timeout); only 418-29 t2 carried real signal.
- 347-49's "delete blank rows secretly also means delete repeated header rows" interpretation is idiosyncratic; I did not add a task-specific rule (would overfit / not generalize). Its type-preservation sub-issue is covered by the general type rule.
